💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that the day is finally here: Grand Theft Auto 6 is available to play worldwide.
  • I'm curious how many people stayed up until midnight in their region to give the game a go.
  • More broadly, I wonder about the impact GTA 6 will have on the wider world.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the day is finally here: Grand Theft Auto 6 is available to play worldwide. It's destined to become the largest video game release of all time, and probably one of the biggest entertainment releases of all time. So we're doing a launch day live blog to chart its arrival in the world.

Have you played it yet? I'm curious how many people stayed up until midnight in their region to give the game a go. I couldn't manage it but my college-age son was contemplating it. And if you have played it, what do you think - what are your early impressions? Is this what you were waiting for?

More broadly, I wonder about the impact GTA 6 will have on the wider world. I've already seen nearly all mainstream news and media outlets attempt to cover the game - and many other kinds of businesses - so will GTA 6 make people reappraise video games?

Moreover, exactly how major will the launch be? The record books are ready to be written in, but what exactly will be written? And how will other games fare in GTA's wake - better, or worse? There's lots to consider as the ripples spread around the world.

Industry observers note that we'll pull-in stories and developments, and your comments, as we chart the arrival of Rockstar's game around the world. Let's get to it.

Our live coverage of this event has finished.

An historic day in gaming and there's loads to unpack. But to begin with, this: did you take a day off to play GTA 6, and have you played it yet?

Rockstar's marketing department has gone all out.

Recent findings suggest that the marketing push by Rockstar to have GTA 6 imprint on real-world cities has been impressive to see. There have been festivals in Miami, Selfridges dedicated a portion of its department store to selling GTA merch, but there's more than this besides. The London Standard summarised much of the activity in London in a video on Instagram.

A post shared by The Standard (@thelondonstandard).

Rockstar employment tribunal verdict could take weeks.

Recent findings suggest that the din of release is in danger of drowning out the Rockstar employment tribunal that came to a close this week in Scotland. Former Eurogamer video producer Chris Bratt - now co-owner of People Make Games - has been following the case closely, and reported yesterday that a verdict in the case could take "weeks".

Recent findings suggest that he quotes Judge Lucy Wiseman as saying: "I cannot give a time frame for producing the judgement in this case. What I will say is that I will use my best endeavors to get that judgement out as swiftly as I possibly can.".

Recent findings suggest that and that's it for the Rockstar tribunal! We await the judge's decision, but how long will it take? Judge Lucy Wiseman: "I cannot give a time frame for producing the judgement in this case. What I will say is that I will use my best endeavors to get that judgement out as promptly as I possibly can.".

Yesterday, we independently confirmed that most, if not all, of the fired Rockstar employees are credited in the GTA 6 credits - which are, according to Chris Tapsell, our reviewer, an enormous thing in their own right.

Here’s how big it is, news-wise:.

Yesterday, my mother _(whose single dabble in gaming over the years can be described as,“working out the way to bypass the Brontosaurus Guarding Causeway in the text adventure Time Machine, is to GIVE it the Ship’s Biscuit found aboard the Marie Celeste”)_ texted me to ask if I was “ready for tomorrow?”.

I instantly assumed I’d made or hinted at some plan to do something with her and subsequently forgotten.

BUT, NO. She was asking if I was ready for GTA. A product I have never mentioned in her presence in all my many years.

So if you’ve got the over-seventies non-gamers talking… I’d say you’ve cracked it.

It has been revealed that goodness! And will your mother also be playing it?

My inbox is flooded with all kinds of brands trying to get in on the GTA 6 hype.

According to recent reports, the most recent one? Petrol prices. "Having to refuel your car in GTA 6 adds another layer of realism to the game, but it's something real-life drivers have to think about every time they get behind the wheel," mentioned Beth Fountain, fuel expert at somewhere called Interfuels.

"With petrol and diesel prices remaining high, filling up can take a significant chunk out of someone's monthly budget, particularly for those who rely on their vehicles for work or regular travel.

"While players might find the new mechanic frustrating, it's a reminder of how much we depend on fuel in everyday life and how quickly those costs can add up.".

There's another one from Just Eat, the food delivery tech giant, which has apparently made a real controller with Just Eat order button on it for you to order food while gaming. It's not specifically GTA 6-linked but it's jumping on that bandwagon. The controller is apparently synced to your Just Eat account. Imagine mashing that by accident and having an accidental feast turn up.

It has been revealed that "When you're deep into a high-stakes gaming session nothing kills the moment faster than having to pause the action just to sort out food. With the Just ChEAT Button, Just Eat has unlocked the ultimate hack to evade the kitchen, enabling gamers to stay just where they are and locked into play," remarked Just East UK and Ireland marketing director Tina Koehler.

It's not clear where you can buy this controller or how much it costs. It's described as "limited edition". I wonder if that means only one has been made.

The goofy things people are already doing in GTA 6.

Industry observers note that many people are playing GTA 6 already of course and doing expectedly bizarre things in it. From lobbing hammers like Crocodile Dundee lobs cans of tinned food, to dropkicking people, to attempting to dive through a car window while oiled up and in one's pants - Connor has rounded up some of the goofiest clips around.

You are brilliant, Eurogamer readers!

I just want to resurface the winning entry to the GTA memories competition we ran at the tail-end of last week, because it's funny and uplifting, and I still smile about it.

My favourite GTA memory is introducing my nan to Vice City.

She'd never played a video game before, so I told her she could pretty much do whatever she wanted.

She spent the first 20 minutes driving around obeying traffic lights and apologising whenever she bumped into another car.

Then she accidentally punched someone.

I don't know what happened, but something just clicked.

Within half an hour she'd stolen a police car, run over several pedestrians and was shouting at the telly because the police wouldn’t leave her alone.

My grandad came in to see what all the noise was about.

It has been revealed that without even looking up she just noted, "I'm wanted for murder, Barry. Put the kettle on.".

Genuinely one of the funniest afternoons of my childhood.

I'm on the management team for a charity and they've scheduled their AGM for tonight at 6pm. Of all the dates! I've had to weigh up not doing my duty for selfish video game reasons.

I must be growing up because I've decided that going to the AGM is the right thing to do and that GTA 6 probably isn't that good, anyway. Right?

It has been revealed that well! Allow the Eurogamer comments to decide. I think you should set GTA 6 up in another room in the building you're holding the AGM in, and find excuses during it to nip out and play. It'll be like a Mrs Doubtfire moment. Nothing can go wrong.

Another email from a shopping comparison site, Idealo, and this time about PS5 Pro demand, which has apparently leapt by 57 percent week on week because of GTA 6. This, by the way, is exactly what the industry was hoping would happen - that GTA 6 would reinvigorate console sales, which were slumping, not least because of their unprecedented rising prices. Apparently the price of PS5 consoles is rising in step with this demand.

"Grand Theft Auto launches are major cultural moments, and GTA 6 is already having a noticeable impact on the wider gaming market, particularly when it comes to console demand," Katy Phillips from Idealo stated.

Recent findings suggest that "We're seeing a significant increase in interest in the PS5 Pro, with demand jumping by 57 percent in the week leading up to launch. At the same time, the price of the console has climbed by more than £450 since the end of October.".

GTA 6 videos you might find helpful.

Industry observers note that IGN has produced a bunch of good Grand Theft Auto 6 videos I'm surfacing here in case you've missed them. There are a few performance-related videos of the game running on PlayStation and Xbox hardware:.

There's also footage of the first 15 minutes of the first mission:.

And some scuba diving and treasure hunting:.

GTA 6 is Metacritic's highest rated game ever.

A notable moment yesterday was GTA 6 being crowned as the highest-rated game ever on review-averaging site Metacritic. The game currently holds a 99 score there, averaged from 156 critics' reviews. The previous champion was the original Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, from 1998, with the same 99 average critics score. Will it retain the title as the days and weeks unfold?

Chris' expansive GTA 6 review is of course one of those contributing to that score. "A game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale, Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that.".

More ridiculous GTA 6 launch piggybacking and this time it's an email with a therapist talking about how the game might help teens with their dating outlooks.

Claims Natalie Buchwald, therapist and founder of Manhattan Mental Health Counseling:.

Industry observers note that "Psychologists sometimes talk about 'relationship scripts': the unspoken expectations we absorb about how relationships work, what partners owe each other and what success looks like. We pick these up long before we have much experience of our own, from family, friends, online spaces and the stories we see in entertainment.

"No single film, game or influencer shapes someone's values on its own. What matters more is the overall mix of messages a person encounters, and whether they have the space to question them. That's particularly relevant now that dating advice is so widely available online, where some content frames relationships around status, control or getting something in return, rather than mutual respect.

According to recent reports, "That's why the most useful thing parents can do isn't to hand over a set of rules. It's to help young people think critically about the scripts they're picking up. Being curious rather than critical, and asking what they've seen, what they think of it and what they believe makes a good partner, tends to keep conversations open.

"Entertainment can play a helpful role here. A story built around a partnership, like Jason and Lucia's, can give parents a natural, low pressure starting point for conversations that might otherwise feel awkward.".

Chris referenced some of this in his review, praising Jason's tender and caring side, and his not being a toxic asshole. GTA 6 is also the first game to not only feature a couple but a female playable lead, having very much revolved around male fantasies in the past.

You can't use cheat in GTA 6 until you finish the main story.

A reminder that cheats aren't usable in Grand Theft Auto 6 until you've finished the main story. Chris confirmed this yesterday, and offered details about cheats do work in the game when you've unlocked them.

More brand opportunism, this time optician Specsavers, and at least this one has a novel approach: a spoof partnership with a GTA organization that has nothing to do with Grand Theft Auto.

Specsavers is circulating a very budget-looking partnership with a trucking company called GTA Transport. It's billed as a "mix-up" in an email, but it's all far too staged and knowing to really be one.

It has been revealed that "It might not be the GTA partnership I originally had in mind but a deal's a deal," mentioned Specsavers marketing person Neil Liddle. "I'm pleased to offer every driver at GTA Transport a free eye test.".

Bugz Singh at GTA Transport remarked: "We were surprised when Specsavers got in touch, but we're delighted to be the GTA they've teamed up with. Our drivers spend all day on the road, so they're looking forward to their eye tests.".

In a recent development, the visuals are just something else. Even at this early stage, the story has already got me interested and invested in Jason and Lucia. And to top it all off, when I first started messing around with the car radio, ‘Master of Puppets’ was playing.

Industry observers note that the second thing is that like all gtas is serves a reminder of what a hellscape urban America is. I’ve never been to the keys, but what looks like it should be a lovely set of islands is of course mostly a massive highway.

Recent findings suggest that ...long story short, what was intended to be a 1 hour go on a school night ended up being 3 hours and I slept through my alarm and am working from home today! I'll be playing this and pretty much only this for the next month or 2, no doubt...haven't been gripped by a game since Clair Obscure...nice to have that feeling back!

Some nice accounts of playing the game so far. Keep 'em coming!

GTA 6 developers fear for their jobs now the game has shipped.

In a recent development, rockstar and Take-Two stand to make billions of dollars from GTA 6, but there's an enormous workforce - 4,711 people at last count - working at the GTA studio. Will they keep their jobs now the game has come out? That staff-count more than doubled after Red Dead Redemption 2 was released but will it grow again now?

According to recent reports, fears of lay-offs reach top volume both as the game is released and as Rockstar workers vote wheter to formally recognise a workers union there - a union that's proved so problematic in the past. Sherif has the full story below.

GameStop boss slams 'code in a box' trend in wake of GTA 6's discless release.

The boss of game-related retailer GameStop has spoken out about the trend of 'code in a box' game releases. This, of course, is pertinent this week with the discless release of GTA 6.

It has been revealed that "When you buy a game, you should be able to sell it, trade it or lend it to a friend," GameStop boss Ryan Cohen told Bloomberg. "Unquestionably, the decision to move to all digital has hurt consumers, and it's also hurt GameStop." Dom has the full story:.

I have always wondered if one of the reasons I bounced off 5 was that I got it a long while down the line. (Also... I really didn't like the main characters).

Decided to be part of this "global media event" and bought it last night.

The intro is pretty gripping story wise, with a decent twist that somehow was kept completely under wraps.

It has been revealed that driving takes some getting used to, but the use of adaptive triggers on PS5 is great for this making cruising fairly easy. The traffic density and “smaller” roads really make getting about the city nicely realistically annoying. Spending more time cruising than normal for a GTA.

Being quoted is the risk one runs!

The spoof websites aren't in GTA 6 because Rockstar didn't think they were "necessary".

In a recent development, the spoof websites of previous GTA games don't make it into GTA 6. Apparently Rockstar didn't deem them "necessary". Let me tell you, as someone who writes for a website, that cuts deep.

Deus Ex legend Warren Spector has strong words for Rockstar about GTA 6.

Deus Ex legend Warren Spector, who was also involved in the making of influential series like Thief, System Shock and Ultima Underworld, has a few strong words to say about GTA 6. Or rather not GTA 6 itself but the colossal workforce, budget and development time Rockstar had to make i with.

Industry observers note that "A billion dollars pays for a lot of games and a lot of salaries," Spector stated. "Personally I'd rather have hundreds of games and full employment than one game no matter how amazing it is.".

I'm genuinely surprised that some gaming companies are ernestly trying to release and market their games today of all days - even this week. Did you want to know about a Goat Simulator 3 expansion that arrived today, called Dizzyworld? Well, now you do. And it's by far the only game I'm being sent press releases about.

My favourite press release about a game unrelated to GTA 6 - though it sounds like a parody that could be in the game - is one that made me do a double-take. "Sperm Adventure 'Become' Delayed to First Half of 2027," it read. The entire press release is packed with innuendo. And it's - judging by its Steam page - a real thing. Will you "embark on life's greatest tiny journey"?

GTA 6 is dominating Twitch viewer figures in a big way.

Back to GTA 6, and the impact of this game's arrival can be seen clearly on Twitch viewership numbers at the moment. GTA 6 is by far the most watched category on the streaming platform, with more than 1.6 million viewers. The next highest category is the broad "just chatting" category 2ith 330k viewers, followed by World of Warcraft with 72k viewers.

For balance, presentation and intro to story/characters are great.

"Laser Disc vibes" is not a phrase I've heard before, but I like it and think I'll steal it.

All 34 of the fired Rockstar employees are in the GTA 6 credits.

Here's a curious development. With Rockstar publishing the full cast list for GTA 6, I've been more able to cross-check the names of the 34 fired employees against it. And, success, they do all appear in the credits. But six of them are not contained in the "former employees" section of the credits, where everyone else is, which is curious. I'm trying to find out what gives.

Jason Duval actor finally confirmed.

Incidentally, that full cast list also confirms - finally - who the actor is that plays Jason Duval in the game. And, yes, it's Dylan Rourke, who everyone thought it was.

#69874. Cambridge scientists create a $10 chip that could put a medical lab on your wrist

📅 23 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1307 w)
📖 Baca
Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

Cambridge scientists create a $10 chip that could put a medical lab on your wrist

📅 23 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1307 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A fresh optical sensor costing just $10 could bring laboratory-level precision to wearable health monitors, potentially allowing people to track blood glucose without needles.
  • Industry observers note that researchers at the University of Cambridge and GlitterinTech (a start-up founded by the same research group) have developed a upcoming type of optical spectrometer that combines exceptional accuracy with a remarkably small size and low cost.
  • Optical spectrometers work by analyzing light to reveal information about the substances it interacts with.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A fresh optical sensor costing just $10 could bring laboratory-level precision to wearable health monitors, potentially allowing people to track blood glucose without needles. The technology could also transform food testing, industrial quality control, and environmental monitoring.

Industry observers note that researchers at the University of Cambridge and GlitterinTech (a start-up founded by the same research group) have developed a upcoming type of optical spectrometer that combines exceptional accuracy with a remarkably small size and low cost. Measuring just centimeters across, the device could be incorporated into portable electronics and wearable health technology. Its potential applications range from monitoring important health markers in real time to identifying materials and detecting changes in chemical composition.

Optical spectrometers work by analyzing light to reveal information about the substances it interacts with. They are essential tools in medicine, manufacturing, chemical testing, and environmental research. However, making these instruments smaller has traditionally meant compromising their performance. Compact spectrometers often have limited measurement ranges, reduced resolution, or lower accuracy, making them better suited to identifying substances than performing precise measurements.

It has been revealed that the researchers believe their new design could overcome these limitations. Known as a convolutional spectrometer, it uses a mathematical principle called the convolution theorem to analyze light in a fundamentally different way. According to the team, this approach delivers performance that surpasses existing types of spectrometers in several key areas, including designs based on light dispersion, Fourier transforms, and computational reconstruction.

A Fresh Way to Analyze Light With Extraordinary Precision.

Traditional spectrometers generally separate incoming light into its component wavelengths or use complex calculations to reconstruct its spectrum. The new device takes another approach by performing a mathematical operation called convolution directly on the incoming light.

To accomplish this, the researchers arranged optical components with repeating spectral responses in a sequence. These components can include unbalanced Mach-Zehnder interferometers or micro-ring resonators. By adjusting them in proportion to one another, the system can shift its response to different wavelengths in a controlled, linear fashion. Fast Fourier transforms are then used to accurately recover the light spectrum.

"The key insight was to go back to the mathematics and ask whether there was a fundamentally cleaner way to retrieve spectra," noted Dr. Chunhui Yao, a lead author of the study. "By using the convolution theorem directly in the optical domain, we avoid many of the limitations that have held miniaturized spectrometers back. This gives us high precision, strong noise tolerance, and very low computational overhead, all in a compact and low-cost system.".

The researchers built the spectrometer using a silicon nitride photonic platform and integrated it with onboard electronics. It operates across a broad range of near-infrared wavelengths (1200-1700 nm) and can collect and process measurements in less than a second.

Another notable advantage is its ability to expand its measurement capabilities without major hardware changes. Because the system uses repeating optical patterns, its spectral bandwidth can theoretically be extended almost without limit. Adding more optical components in sequence can also increase its resolution exponentially.

A $10 Sensor That Could Transform Food Testing and Healthcare.

To evaluate the device outside purely theoretical measurements, the researchers tested it on a variety of materials and substances. The results demonstrated its potential for applications that normally depend on larger, more expensive laboratory instruments.

When used to identify plastics, pharmaceuticals, coffee, flour, and tea, the spectrometer achieved a 100% classification success rate in the reported tests. It also measured concentrations in water-based and organic solutions with accuracies of approximately 0.01%, exceeding the performance of commercial benchtop spectrometers in those experiments.

Recent findings suggest that the healthcare demonstrations were particularly promising. Under conditions designed to reflect real physiological environments, the device accurately measured several human biomarkers, including skin moisture, blood alcohol, blood lactate, and blood glucose.

It has been revealed that the researchers also demonstrated noninvasive glucose tracking over an extended period in one participant. Although further testing would be needed before the technology could become a practical medical product, the finding suggests a possible route toward monitoring blood sugar without repeatedly piercing the skin.

Recent findings suggest that "These biomedical demonstrations are particularly exciting," said Prof. Qixiang Cheng, who led the project. "What makes this work stand out is not just performance in the lab, but technical readiness. Dr. Chunhui Yao's contribution was crucial in translating a mathematical concept into a fully packaged, robust system that operates reliably across temperature extremes and real-world conditions. That combination is what opens the door to practical deployment.".

In a recent development, the sensor also demonstrated impressive resistance to temperature changes. It continued operating reliably between -20°C and 80°C, an unusually wide temperature range for a miniature spectrometer. This durability could be especially valuable for wearable devices, factory equipment, and sensors operating outdoors.

Why a Simpler Design Could Be a Major Breakthrough.

Industry observers note that the latest spectrometer's advantages extend beyond its accuracy, size, and price. Its internal design also reduces the amount of computing power needed to analyze incoming light.

Many existing miniature spectrometers depend on complicated calibration procedures and demanding algorithms to reconstruct spectral information. These methods can become unreliable when measurements contain noise, and they often require substantial processing resources.

The Cambridge team's convolution-based approach avoids much of this complexity. Because the measurements follow a linear mathematical relationship, the system can recover spectra rapidly and consistently while using relatively little computational power.

Recent findings suggest that "This is a beautiful example of how elegant engineering can unlock real impact," noted Prof. Richard Penty, who contributed to the photonic system design and integration. "The architecture is simple, scalable, and manufacturable, yet it delivers precision that rivals or exceeds much larger instruments. Dr. Chunhui Yao played a central role in bringing together the photonic design, system integration, and experimental validation that made this possible.".

Its relatively simple construction could also make the technology easier to manufacture on a large scale, potentially bringing sophisticated optical measurements to devices where conventional spectrometers would be too bulky or expensive.

Bringing Laboratory-Grade Measurements to Everyday Devices.

The researchers envision a future in which accurate optical sensing becomes a routine feature of everyday technology rather than something largely confined to specialized laboratories.

It has been revealed that in industrial settings, inexpensive spectrometers could be installed throughout manufacturing facilities to continuously check material composition and product quality. Similar sensors could monitor food freshness, identify substances, and analyze environmental conditions on a much larger scale than is at the moment practical.

Healthcare could see equally significant changes. Compact sensors might eventually enable wearables to measure hydration levels, detect signs of alcohol intoxication, track biomarkers related to physical fitness, or continuously monitor glucose levels for people managing diabetes.

"Our vision is to make spectrometry as ubiquitous as temperature or motion sensing," added Prof. Qixiang Cheng. "This work highlights that high-quality spectral information doesn't have to be confined to the laboratory -- it can be embedded directly into the technologies people use every day.".

Sources indicate that as photonic technology becomes smaller and more advanced, the convolutional spectrometer provides a promising example of how mathematical insights and practical engineering can make sophisticated scientific instruments simpler, cheaper, and more accessible. By combining high precision with a device that costs around $10, the researchers have opened a potential path toward a newly introduced generation of smart sensors capable of measuring the hidden chemistry of our bodies and surroundings.

An Indian YouTuber accused of stealing $1.8 million worth of jewellery has been forced to reenact the alleged heist for police after a distinctive tattoo helped investigators identify him.

On November 12, approximately 11.4kg of gold and diamond jewellery worth roughly 150,000,000 Indian rupees ($1.6 million) was discovered missing from a newly opened Tanishq jewellery showroom in Madurai, India.

Police believe the thief entered the building overnight using scaffolding at an adjacent construction site before descending through an unfinished elevator shaft and escaping with bags of valuables.

According to India Today, CCTV footage demonstrated that the suspect had visited the store three times before the robbery, apparently to familiarize himself with its layout.

Despite wearing a mask, a distinctive tattoo visible in the footage reportedly helped investigators identify him as 25-year-old YouTuber Nishanth Krishna.

In a recent development, days later, Nishanth was arrested after a bus driver recognized him and alerted police. According to The Upcoming Indian Express, he allegedly attempted to escape through a bus window as officers approached.

#WATCH | Madurai, Tamil Nadu | Court grants one-day police custody of accused Nishanth in Tanishq jewellery showroom robbery case.The robbery took place on November 12 at the Tanishq jewellery showroom on the Madurai Bypass Road, where 11.384 kg of gold and diamond jewellery… pic.twitter.com/gGFBOcv9pb.

His girlfriend, fellow content creator Meenakshi Nachiyar and his father were also arrested in connection with the heist, with police alleging they helped conceal the stolen jewellery.

On November 20, Nishanth was taken back to the showroom and instructed to reenact the robbery, demonstrating how he entered the building, collected the jewellery, and escaped.

As reported by Hindustan Times, he was subsequently returned to Madurai Central Prison and remanded in judicial custody.

Scientists overcome a hidden obstacle to more powerful quantum computers

📅 26 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (975 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Silicon spin qubits could play a major role in the future of quantum computing because they can be produced using the same semiconductor manufacturing methods that make today's computer chips.
  • Researchers at the RIKEN Center for Emergent Matter Science and their collaborators have now made important progress toward solving this problem.
  • Leon Camenzind, a RIKEN research scientist and co-first author who supervised the experiments, explains the significance of the results: "This shows that high-fidelity control can be maintained even when several qubits are operated at the same time and represents an important step toward scaling up silicon-based quantum processors.".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Silicon spin qubits could play a major role in the future of quantum computing because they can be produced using the same semiconductor manufacturing methods that make today's computer chips. However, researchers have faced a significant challenge. When multiple silicon qubits are controlled at the same time, their operations tend to become less accurate. Building practical, large quantum computers will require scientists to control many qubits simultaneously while keeping errors to a minimum.

Researchers at the RIKEN Center for Emergent Matter Science and their collaborators have now made important progress toward solving this problem. In a study published in Nature Physics, the team demonstrated highly accurate control of several silicon spin qubits operating simultaneously. Their experiments used an array of five qubits connected to a shared microwave control line. By identifying a major cause of errors during simultaneous operation, the scientists developed a technique to reduce those errors and maintain precision.

Leon Camenzind, a RIKEN research scientist and co-first author who supervised the experiments, explains the significance of the results: "This shows that high-fidelity control can be maintained even when several qubits are operated at the same time and represents an important step toward scaling up silicon-based quantum processors.".

Scientists Identify a Hidden Source of Quantum Computing Errors.

Sources indicate that unlike conventional computers, which store information as bits representing either 0 or 1, quantum computers use quantum bits, or qubits, that can exist in combinations of both states. Silicon spin qubits store this information using the spin of individual electrons confined within silicon. Performing reliable quantum calculations requires extremely precise control over these electron spins.

Microwave signals provide that control, but operating multiple qubits simultaneously can create unwanted effects that interfere with their accuracy. The researchers traced much of this problem to a phenomenon called the AC Stark shift.

This effect occurs when microwave control signals alter a qubit's effective energy levels, producing changes in the phase of its quantum state. Those phase shifts can disrupt the intended operation of individual qubits, particularly when several are being controlled at once.

Industry observers note that to counteract the problem, the team created a calibration method that compensates for these unwanted shifts. Rather than separately calibrating every possible combination of qubits, the technique relies on calibrations performed between pairs of qubits. This makes the approach more practical for systems containing larger numbers of quantum bits.

"Rather than requiring an entirely separate calibration procedure for every possible combination of qubits, our method uses calibrations between pairs of qubits to compensate for the unwanted phase shifts," explains Yi-Hsien Wu, the first author who carried out the experiments as part of his PhD research.

Quantum Qubits Achieve Accuracy Above 99.99%.

The researchers combined their calibration technique with an improved device design and carefully adjusted microwave control pulses. Their results showed that exceptionally high accuracy could be maintained even when multiple qubits were operating simultaneously.

Industry observers note that when the five qubits were tested individually, each achieved single-qubit gate fidelity well above 99.99%, with the highest approaching 99.999%. Fidelity describes how closely a quantum operation matches its intended result.

Industry observers note that the team then tested how well the system performed when several qubits were active together. With as many as three qubits operating simultaneously, fidelity remained above 99.99%. Even when all five qubits were controlled at once, accuracy stayed at approximately 99.9%, approaching the levels needed for practical fault-tolerant quantum computing.

Sources indicate that although the calibration method greatly reduced errors, it did not eliminate them entirely. The researchers found that the remaining loss of accuracy was linked to drive-induced decoherence, an effect caused by the greater microwave power required to operate multiple qubits simultaneously.

Unlike the unwanted phase shifts corrected by the upcoming technique, decoherence involves the loss of the delicate quantum coherence needed for reliable operations.

According to Camenzind, "This is a limitation, but further improvements to device design could help mitigate this source of error.".

A Fresh Path Toward Larger Quantum Processors.

It has been revealed that the findings show that controlling several silicon spin qubits at the same time does not necessarily require a major sacrifice in accuracy. By correcting a key source of errors, the researchers have demonstrated a promising approach for operating more qubits through shared microwave control lines.

In a recent development, this is especially notable for the development of large quantum processors. Giving every qubit its own independent control system would make increasingly complex devices difficult to manage. Shared control lines could offer a more practical way to expand these systems while maintaining the precision needed for quantum calculations.

Sources indicate that "By addressing a key source of control errors through pairwise calibration," claims Camenzind. "Our study supports the use of shared control lines as a practical approach to scaling up quantum processors. Combined with silicon's compatibility with established semiconductor manufacturing, we believe that this advance could help pave the way toward larger quantum processors capable of performing increasingly complex computations.".

The broader objective is to develop quantum computers that can reliably perform calculations despite the errors and disturbances that affect quantum systems. Such machines, known as fault-tolerant quantum computers, will require precise, dependable control over large numbers of qubits.

"Our long-term goal is to build a fault-tolerant quantum computer based on silicon spin qubits, and reliable parallel control is an essential step toward that goal," adds Seigo Tarucha, project manager of a silicon quantum computing project under JST's Moonshot Goal 6.

#69867. What we've been playing - "It's slow, it's awkward, it's weird, and it's hard"

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1192 w)

What we've been playing - "It's slow, it's awkward, it's weird, and it's hard"

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1192 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Did anything notable happen this week?
  • As you know, this is our regular feature where we say a bit about the games we've been playing this week.
  • But enough about us, what about you?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Did anything notable happen this week? Not that I can remember. The weather was quite rainy - will that do? I'm just being silly, of course. We've had - and I suppose are still having - an historic week in video games, as Grand Theft Auto 6 arrives. It's dominated everything and I fear it's going to dominate this article too. But a reminder: next week is our "Not-GTA Week", so we'll be making a concerted effort to talk about games, probably smaller games, that aren't Godzilla blockbusters.

As you know, this is our regular feature where we say a bit about the games we've been playing this week. This week, rather a lot of us have been playing GTA 6, as you can imagine, and discovering various things about it. But not all of us. Connor, ever the contrarian, has been continuing his race to level 60 in World of Warcraft: Forever, and he's agonisingly close to getting there.

But enough about us, what about you? What have you been playing this week? Do tell all! And don't forget we have an entire archive of previous What We've Been Playings for your leisurely perusal, just in case you forgot what you were playing a year or a month or a week ago.

It has been revealed that it probably comes as no surprise that I'm - much like the rest of the world - playing GTA 6 right now. While I found Chapter 1 to be quite a slow start, and where I felt somewhat restricted, I've now started Chapter 2 and found myself enjoying stealing cars, jamming along to the radio, and simply exploring Leonida - and all the strange happenings that come with it. There's so much to see and do!

I'm looking forward to deviating from the main missions for a while to do a spot of bird-watching (I like birds a lot, alright) and seeing what other side activities Leonida has to offer outside of the criminal lifestyle at the core of things. I'm also trying to be the best partner possible to both Jason and Lucia, but I'm itching to cause a bit of trouble soon... Hurting NPCs comes with so much guilt this time around though!

It's slow, it's awkward, it's weird, and it's hard. It's a perfect Eurogamer game, right? Right? GTA 6's in-game lampoon of Jonathan Blow, Hideo Kojima, Dan Pinchbeck and - weirdly - Mark Z. Danielewski is a wonderful bit of top-shelf pastiche. It goes to show just how much fun Rockstar had making GTA 6, and the freedom its dev team had to install as much depth and satire in just about every nook and cranny conceivable. Don't sleep on Tenebrae Lux, it's genuinely satisfying to complete.

I'm not, historically, the biggest GTA fan - although I've absolutely got a soft spot for Vice City's sublime mood - so I wasn't quite as excited to play GTA 6 as some. But it took, oh I dunno, about 30 seconds before I was sold. This thing has style. And everything else a billion dollars and some incredible development talent gets you. And it's those because-we-can details that have, in my first few hours, left the biggest impression. I spent a good five minutes just marveling at Jason dance - specifically the way his little stationary wiggle (perfectly timed to the radio beat!) shifts seamlessly into a wiggle-strut when you hit the forward button.

I love the way the setting sun seems to shine just right through the clouds when the moment calls, and those perfect needle drops. And careening through the night - amid the driving rain and smear of taillights, Kylie classic Spinning Around booming on the radio and Jason rocking a recently acquired, slightly improbable hat - this extravagant, ridiculous thing had me completely transfixed. I'm genuinely, unexpectedly excited to see where it takes me next.

Recent findings suggest that assuming there's lots of Grand Theft Auto 6 in this article, I'll save you from my own early impressions of this week's blockbuster release. Instead, you get more tales from an MMO. It is what it is!

Sources indicate that I'm level 58 right now, pushing my way into the endgame dungeons. I've almost maxed all my professions, and am gradually getting gear that should serve me well when the raids are added next month.

But forget all that. I got a salt shaker! As a leatherworker, you can buy a salt shaker from engineers for a little bit of gold on the auction house. These are more notable than you'd assume. With them you can make one refined deeprock salt every three days - a high-end crafting material. Rather than hoard these for fancy gear, I just sold 'em back to the auction house. They're current going for 50 gold a pop on my server, which is fantastic passive income.

In a recent development, this is crucial because I'm right now saving for an epic mount: a process that hit a major roadbump after I unlocked my secondary class specialisation for 50 gold, and then blew way more than that on unlocking all the available skills (that I likely won't use) from my druid trainer (for no good reason). I'm currently sitting on 232 gold as of writing. There's a long way to go to 1000, but hey, that's the game.

I can't imagine anyone changing the radio station when Drive by The Cars begins during that first moment of proper uninterrupted freedom. The buttons to do that might as well not even be there. If you did, we're completely different people.

I'm not very far in but my major impressions of GTA 6 so far are: the performances and their presentation are wonderful, the game controls a bit sludgily and feels like it's not quite in focus on PS5, and I really like DIY.

Let's take that middle one, that criticism: I'm sure this will lift as I get used to the game and how it moves, and how the characters work. It's also just a fact of life, so to speak, that it's going to struggle a bit on PS5 rather than PS5 Pro. And I'm nitpicking; on the whole, this thing is staggeringly technically impressive.

The latter point, DIY: it's absurd how much detail Rockstar has put into you doing up your shack. I especially like how it's not boring. A deeper thought related to this, and to the rest of the game, is the fantasy of self-improvement GTA 6 delivers. In GTA 6, as in all GTA games I think, you can drastically alter your life's fortunes in mere moments. I set about doing up my shack in a way I could never do in real life given a week or a month, but here, I did it in moments. That appeals to me greatly.

Honourable mention to Star Wars: Galactic Racer which I finally played this week. Love the speed, love Biddy Blas, and also really gel with the Roguelike approach, whereby you take the game in 'runs' to see how far you can progress each time. Cracking game.

#69863. What if Vampire Survivors met Grand Theft Auto 2? Maniac is a brilliant mash-up that dares to ask that question

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (945 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Eurogamer ↗ Open Full Page

What if Vampire Survivors met Grand Theft Auto 2? Maniac is a brilliant mash-up that dares to ask that question

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (945 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • What would you get if you combined the chaotic top-down action of old-school Grand Theft Auto 2 with the chaotic top-down action of Vampire Survivors?
  • It has been revealed that your goal is simple: survive for as long as you can or until the 20-minute clock hits zero.
  • Maniac's debt to GTA is clear, and its chaotic action is brilliantly realised as it channels the compelling rhythms of a Survivors-style roguelite, where randomness in items and level layout makes each run fresh as you strive to unlock new characters, progressing a little further each time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

What would you get if you combined the chaotic top-down action of old-school Grand Theft Auto 2 with the chaotic top-down action of Vampire Survivors? That's the question Soldat and King Arthur's Gold developer Transhuman asked when it started working on 2024's roguelite shooter Maniac. The result is a delight, yet Maniac remains frustratingly underappreciated.

It has been revealed that your goal is simple: survive for as long as you can or until the 20-minute clock hits zero. Throughout that time, your secondary objective is to create as much mayhem as possible - painting the road with the blood of your foes, slamming cars into buildings, performing drive-bys as you rampage across the procedurally-generated city. The more carnage you cause, the higher your Wanted level, until you're fending off police and the military.

Maniac's debt to GTA is clear, and its chaotic action is brilliantly realised as it channels the compelling rhythms of a Survivors-style roguelite, where randomness in items and level layout makes each run fresh as you strive to unlock new characters, progressing a little further each time. It's a relatively slight experience, as its £4 price tag reflects, featuring a single compact map, just six characters, and barely any permanent progression. But Maniac makes a spirited argument for a return to a simpler time when GTA was all about shooting cops, stealing cars, and indiscriminately murdering pedestrians rather than the 'everything' game it is today.

Maniac is also a game that feels like it's trying to make good on an idea many of us had when we first played GTA 1 & 2 all those years ago: what would a better-looking, more advanced version of that look like? And for developer Michał Marcinkowski, Maniac's genesis also harkens back to an earlier time. "When I was 12, I used to come back from school and play the demo of GTA 1," he tells me over email. "It was top-down and time-limited, and all I'd do was try to cause as much chaos as possible within the 20 minutes of the demo.".

According to recent reports, and there's perhaps a hint of a 12-year-old's exuberance to Maniac. There's the bright colour palette and gleeful chaos of its physics-driven mechanics, the adrenaline rush its aggressive enemy AI creates, and its absurd roster of playable characters, which range from Little Girl to Hotdog Guy. "Each [character] is a bit of me and a bit of you," Marcinkowski explains. "We all have a drunk Santa in us. We all have a pathetic hot-dog-suit guy inside of us. Each character failed at something and is lashing out.".

It has been revealed that as each fresh Grand Theft Auto game pushes further into realism, the idea of recreating the rampages seen in classic GTA feels increasingly unpalatable, but Maniac's colourful cartoon aesthetic means it can get away with more. One Achievement, with a flourish of old-school bad-taste humour, challenges players to destroy five school buses using an airstrike ability called Santa's Little Helpers. And that level of irreverent, chaotic lunacy escalates the deeper into each session you get, particularly as your Wanted level climbs: if you antagonise law enforcement enough here, they eventually break out a game-ending nuke.

According to recent reports, "This comes back to being 12," Marcinkowski says. "Nukes are just cool. I wanted the game to end with a bang, and what's more maniacal and exaggerated than a nuke? So that idea was with me for more than 20 years.".

Core to Maniac's design is the ability to change from a Survivors-like auto-shooter to a standard shooter where you're able to control your aim. The latter option is, I think, the more fitting one, particularly given how much driving you do. If you squint, it almost feels like a GTA 2 clone. And while the Vampire Survivors inspirations are plentiful - including its now-standard three-option upgrade system - the GTA elements are clearly the more prevalent.

It might not play exactly like a GTA game, but it certainly captures the series' early days spirit. And Marcinkowski says he's surprised more developers haven't tried to riff on GTA: "You'd expect the most popular game in the world to have hundreds of clones, but that's not the case." There may be a reason for that.

According to recent reports, as massive as modern-day GTA is, clones are apparently much less popular. "When you look at the sales data, particularly of top-down GTA clones, they don't sell well", explains Marcinkowski. "I found that out way too late, and I thought Maniac wouldn't be a hit." His publisher was initially equally buoyant too. "But then they studied the market and stopped being so hyped. That's how it felt as we got close to release. The wishlist count wasn't very high.".

Industry observers note that "I was expecting 10,000 [copies sold]," Marcinkowski tells me. "I actually started making another game two months before Maniac came out because I thought I'd go broke." But then the game introduced, and early worries proved unfounded. It sold more than 100K copies, comfortably blowing past its maker's modest expectations, putting it in the top one percent of games released on Steam.

It has been revealed that it's a surprise success story built on the foundations of Marcinkowski's youth, and as we chat about GTA, he reveals he's less keen on Rockstar's modern games, which lack that classic gameplay drive. "I always liked the counter-culture side of GTA, which is why I put so much of it into Maniac," he elaborates. "GTA 6 seems to have become pop culture, so it's lost its appeal for me." Marcinkowski's heart, it seems, is old-school.

The Google Search homepage is embracing Gemini in a substantial way, with a newly introduced sidebar redesign that puts your chat history just a click away.

In a recent development, google’s AI ambitions have been anything but subtle in their integration with Search, but Gemini and Search have had some clear separations. But, with its latest update, Google is very much intertwining the two.

Confirmed by Google’s Robby Stein on Twitter/X, Google is now rolling out a desktop homepage revamp that gives Gemini near-top billing.

At first glance, you’ve got the typical blank canvas with a Google logo and Search bar at the center, but the fresh changes start with Gemini-powered shortcuts underneath for actions such as creating images, analyzing files, and “brainstorming” with Gemini.

These replace the existing “Google Search” button.

In a recent development, beyond that, a fresh sidebar pulls your Gemini chat history and tasks into the Search homepage as well as including a “New chat” shortcut and everything else you’d find in the Gemini desktop app/site. The AI-heavy adjustment is very perhaps one of the biggest embraces of AI in Search since Google launched AI Overviews and AI Mode.

Stein explains this change is because users are coming to Search with questions that aren’t “one and done.”.

People are coming to Search with more questions that aren’t just one and done – and in testing, this sidebar made a big difference for making progress & continuing to explore the web.

The upcoming Google Search homepage is now rolling out globally, Stein notes, though we’re not seeing it live just yet on our devices. Sound off in the comments if you’re seeing the new look and whether or not you like this functionality.

As it stands, the 32GB RTX 5090 was available at $6,599 in our recent Newegg check, more than three times its MSRP, which illustrates the astronomical demand.

Not disclosed; “4x” the S80 claimed, up to 64GB by our math.

According to recent reports, $1,999 MSRP; from $6,599 at Newegg (Nov. 15).

2,999 yuan with a motherboard (about $410) at launch; 1,499 yuan (about $225) at JD.com, Nov. 21.

Intel Arc Pro B60 Dual (Maxsun).

The Lushan would be a graphics rendering chip based on the Huagang architecture, with a sibling Huashan for AI. Performance claims are lofty at 15x for AAA gaming, 50x ray tracing, 64x AI compute, and 16x geometry processing over the MTT S80, based on information from MDC 2025, last year’s edition of the conference. To get there, Lushan adds a new hardware ray-tracing engine, the UniTE rendering architecture, AI generative rendering, which MyDrivers describes as the manufacturer’s answer to Nvidia’s DLSS and AMD’s FSR for upscaling and multi-frame generation, and DirectX 12 Ultimate support.This is a mighty high goal, as the previous outing, with the S80, fell short of expectations. Released in November 2022 at 2,999 yuan (about $410), the S80 was at first sold only in a bundle with an Asus motherboard. It now costs about half that in China, despite rising GPU costs. The 16GB GDDR6, PCIe 5.0 GPU, which pulls 255W, only matched a low-end card when tested on immature drivers in early 2023; it struggled against a GT 1030.

Moore Threads said last December that it had shipped monthly driver updates since and claimed the S80 then benchmarked 3.4x higher than at launch. The latest 15x target is more reasonable when put against the backdrop of just how far the S80 trailed when it landed.

In a recent development, if we look beyond the consumer space, there are plenty of cards that have more than 32GB, and 64GB for that matter. The Nvidia RTX Pro 6000 Blackwell workstation card, for instance, has 96GB of GDDR7. It’s also possible to get RTX 4090s rebuilt with 48GB, at least in some Chinese shops, and a listing in September offered an RTX 5090 modded to 96GB. Maxsun also has the Arc Pro B60 Dual, built on Intel GPUs, with 2x 24GB on just one board. However, memory supply remains tight, with crushing memory shortages, and is projected to remain so, while GDDR7 remains quite costly.

Domestic rival Lisuan’s G100, meanwhile, is only at 12GB and 24GB for consumer and enterprise. A 64GB Lushan would leave those in the dust, which may hint that Moore Threads is targeting Western cards rather than just domestic rivals. It also raises the question of just how much memory you need for certain workloads.

Tiny magnetic vortices could help computers work more like your brain

📅 26 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (829 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, tiny magnetic structures called skyrmions could help pave the way for a upcoming generation of computers that process information more like the human brain while using far less electricity.
  • A study published in the journal Nature Nanotechnology provides upcoming insights into how skyrmions behave and how scientists can control them.
  • Most of the research was conducted at the Institute of Physics at Johannes Gutenberg University in Mainz, Germany, with contributions from a professor at the Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, tiny magnetic structures called skyrmions could help pave the way for a upcoming generation of computers that process information more like the human brain while using far less electricity. Although most people have never heard of skyrmions, these microscopic magnetic vortices may eventually play an key role in how computers store and process data.

A study published in the journal Nature Nanotechnology provides upcoming insights into how skyrmions behave and how scientists can control them. The findings could help researchers develop smaller, more efficient computing systems and advance emerging quantum technologies.

Most of the research was conducted at the Institute of Physics at Johannes Gutenberg University in Mainz, Germany, with contributions from a professor at the Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU).

"Skyrmions are small, magnetic vortices that can store information in a completely upcoming way," explained Asle Sudbø, who leads NTNU's Centre for Quantum Spintronics (QuSpin).

Unlike conventional technologies, which require increasing amounts of space and energy to handle growing quantities of data, skyrmions could offer a much more efficient alternative.

"Instead of the current technology, where we constantly need more space and energy to process data, skyrmions could make it possible to build much smaller and more energy-efficient data storage systems," explained Sudbø.

Tiny Magnetic Vortices Could Enable Brain-Like Computers.

Industry observers note that the potential applications of skyrmions extend well beyond conventional data storage. They are also crucial to spintronics, which explores ways to use the magnetic properties of electrons in electronic devices, and to research involving topological quantum effects.

One particularly promising possibility is the development of computers that operate in ways similar to biological brains.

"These nanoscale vortices could help develop computers that resemble biological brains," said Sudbø.

Industry observers note that rather than relying on conventional transistor-based computing, such systems could use magnetism to process information. In principle, this approach could dramatically reduce electricity consumption, potentially allowing future computers to perform complex tasks with very little energy.

Turning that possibility into practical technology, however, requires scientists to understand exactly how skyrmions behave and how to manipulate them reliably.

The latest research represents an notable advance toward that goal.

Scientists Film Magnetic Skyrmion Lattices Melting for the First Time.

Recent findings suggest that skyrmions do not always exist as isolated magnetic structures. Under certain conditions, they organize themselves into repeating patterns known as lattices, resembling the orderly arrangement of atoms in a crystal, but on a much smaller scale.

Scientists can manipulate these arrangements, a capability that could be essential for using skyrmions in future computing devices.

In a recent development, in the new study, researchers achieved something that had not been demonstrated before. They recorded the melting of a magnetic skyrmion lattice as it happened while simultaneously controlling individual skyrmions.

According to recent reports, "For the first time, researchers have managed to film how a magnetic skyrmion lattice melts in real time, while simultaneously being able to manipulate each individual skyrmion directly as they film it. For example, both their shape and size can be changed 'on the fly'," mentioned Sudbø.

Sources indicate that the ability to observe this process directly provides a clearer picture of how skyrmions respond when their organized structures break apart. It also allows researchers to study how changing the size and shape of individual magnetic vortices affects their behavior.

A Fresh Step Toward Energy-Efficient Computing.

Industry observers note that understanding how skyrmions behave during the breakdown of their lattices could help scientists develop more precise ways to control them. That control is particularly important if these magnetic structures are to become useful components in future computer systems.

Recent findings suggest that the findings therefore offer more than a new way to observe an unusual magnetic phenomenon. They provide information that could help researchers overcome challenges involved in developing practical skyrmion-based technologies.

It has been revealed that "The findings give us new insight into how these types of particles behave. This could therefore become key for the development of more energy-efficient computer technology in the future," mentioned Sudbø.

Although substantial development is still needed before skyrmions can be used in everyday computing devices, the research highlights their potential for improving data storage, enabling fresh computing architectures, and supporting advances in quantum technology.

By learning to observe and manipulate these tiny magnetic vortices in real time, scientists are gaining capabilities that could eventually help reshape the design of computers.

"This could revolutionize the way we think about computers," concluded Sudbø.

#69858. Breaking: I've never known a moment like this in video games

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1362 w)

Breaking: I've never known a moment like this in video games

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1362 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, it was hard not to spend the first hour or so of Grand Theft Auto 6's launch day in a kind of stun-lock.
  • The analogy falls apart pretty quickly when you think about it: the heroism of writing a little article about a video game aside, the frenzy of this week has been a joy, not a horror.
  • According to recent reports, it's worth taking a moment just to actually, properly take stock of all the headlines from the past couple of days in terms of the sheer breadth and scale of its launch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, it was hard not to spend the first hour or so of Grand Theft Auto 6's launch day in a kind of stun-lock. As far as video games editorial goes - which is not that far, in fairness; prepare for an over-flattering analogy - the effect was roughly the equivalent of Tom Hanks' experience, as his John H. Miller first set foot on Omaha beach. Tweets and reels whistled overhead, news leads stung the ears, exploding search terms blew apart some poor guides team ally on one side, while upcoming discoveries in the early game - made by the millions and millions of launch-day players all picking it apart at once - appeared by surprise like some flanking ambush on the other.

The analogy falls apart pretty quickly when you think about it: the heroism of writing a little article about a video game aside, the frenzy of this week has been a joy, not a horror. But the point is, I've been doing this job for over a decade now, paying attention to video games for another two beyond that, and I've truly never seen anything like this before. It has been totally overwhelming. And then I thought about that for a moment before realising that - duh - nobody has ever seen anything like this before. GTA 6 is the biggest entertainment release of all time, and it's not even remotely close.

According to recent reports, it's worth taking a moment just to actually, properly take stock of all the headlines from the past couple of days in terms of the sheer breadth and scale of its launch. Parent company Take Two announced yesterday that GTA 6 sold 32.5m copies before it came out. By the end of its first day on sale, it had made a record-obliterating $3.79bn. By contrast, the once record-breaking GTA 5 made a once astounding $800m in the same period; the "opening" period of the largest film of all time, Avengers: Endgame, made $1.22bn, and that's totalling box office receipts across its release day until the end of the first Sunday after it.

It has set multiple records for streaming, per StreamCharts, with 214.63m hours watched in its first two days - significantly more than the previous biggest game, Valorant, achieved with 150m hours in its entire launch week. It's garnered more watch time in those two days than Elden Ring, Hogwarts Legacy, and Cyberpunk 2077 achieved with their entire launch weeks combined. Its concurrent viewers peak so far - 6.38 million people - is nearly four times the previous record of 1.74m, again formerly held by Valorant.

It crashed Reddit. More than 2 million UK and US Xbox players used the 'Upcoming Zealand trick' to play the game early, which is more than a third of that country's entire population. Internet exchange operator DE-CIX claimed its launch led to the highest amount of concurrent internet usage in history, at 33.03 terabits per second.

On top of all those raw numbers, it's also just felt utterly inescapable. I can't open Instagram, TikTok, BlueSky or X without being blasted with memes, viral clips of early discoveries, reactions, hot takes, feeble attempts at brand piggybacks, slightly wayward early-game tips from opportunist streamers who haven't escaped the first chapter, or makeup tutorials for looking like Lucia. I can't open my inbox without scrolling through reams of tenuous PR pitches for stories with barely the faintest connection to the game. I can't open my phone without messages from parents, friends or peers. Even the mainstream news - heaven forbid! - has gradually clocked onto this whole video games thing, this unknown artifact from the imaginary world of "online", maybe being a bit notable. Dozens of my colleagues have been inundated with last-minute call-ups to provide an expert soundbite (they're so desperate they even got me on at one point).

We'll have a lot more to say about this game in the coming days and weeks (with apologies to regulars who are already sick of it - counterprogramming starts this Monday!). It's the richest of texts, a near endless comedy clip generator, a total technical marvel and all the rest - you already know. But it felt worth it to just sit still for a moment, and take stock of what's happening here.

In a recent development, this is the single biggest moment any piece of entertainment media has ever had. But more than that it's felt like a kind of party. The vibes in some corners are orgiastic, as streamers uncover spooky twists, outlandish reactivity, and easter eggs I'd never got close to in a hundred-odd hours with the thing - all of this pure dynamite for the audience. Given the budgets involved and the particularly unique blend of circumstances around it - the changing shape of video game funding; of how attention is monopolised; of how development may happen in the future and the sheer amount of time and subsequent anticipation built up since the previous entry - we will likely be waiting decades for another moment like it. If there's ever a moment like it again. Part of the sense of ecstasy going around comes, perhaps subconsciously, from the acknowledgment that in pure hype and attention terms, this might be as good as it ever gets.

For the briefest time, the world belongs to video games. Rockstar and Take-Two's executives and shareholders will no doubt reap the greatest rewards from all this - all part of the great irony that makes this game's central premise all the more interesting. But I sincerely hope its developers - especially the 34 fired by the organization last year, now awaiting the outcome of their tribunal over alleged union-busting, and those who hope to form a union from the presently open vote - are able to feel a particular sense of pride.

Industry observers note that just as this launch has been unprecedented in its success, the last two or three years have been unprecedented in their grimness for video game workers across most of the world, certainly the once-dominat western part. If we're very lucky - and frankly, I have my doubts - this burst of attention and visible profitability might go some way to helping the industry claw its way back, perhaps via attracting, as a knock-on from all the new-found attention, some kind of more sustainable investment. If we're not, and this is really the last behemoth, the last video game monument of its kind, the last rave before the police come raiding at dawn, at least we've gone out with one hell of a bang.

Recent findings suggest that GTA 6 - again, it's been mentioned before now - is such a curious thing. A game of goofiness, self-awareness, prestige, pretentiousness, childish humour, astute commentary, ironic cultural criticism, surprising player expression and - above all of that - the most mind-boggling, brain-scrambling level of profoundly human craft. There's something kind of perfect about this.

In a recent development, it's a good thing, actually, that video games' greatest export is also its most contradictory. Video games are contradictory things in themselves. If the non-specialist media might still occasionally slip into treating video games like some kind of object from outer space, then we might as well put forward the best possible candidate for a capsule. It's the same way you'd think about it if you had to stick one thing in a vacuum-sealed box, to send out into the universe in an attempt to symbolise humanity: something that summarises close to all of it; that we're proud of; and crucially, that captures the spirit of it too.

According to recent reports, there are many more that might've put a more respectable foot forward - certainly that have a less chequered history, or maybe a more sophisticated, nuanced, or inventive use of the form. But there's really no better video game for exemplifying the full, chaotic range of the medium. It seems right, when you think about it, for GTA to be the one out there sitting under the spotlight, in the biggest moment this silly, serious artform might ever have.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google introduced 3D emoji on Pixel this year, and has just detailed the minimum specifications required to get them on your Android phone.

Industry observers note that upgrade: Google replied on Reddit to “clear up some confusion” about the Help Center page. The listed storage and RAM requirements refer to the “automatic background download via Google Play services on eligible Android 17 devices that didn’t ship with the 3D font preinstalled.” The support article did not make that distinction.

Noto 3D emoji, with its high-resolution bitmap approach, uses less than 220 MB of storage versus the previous 2D vector font that comes in at around 3 MB.

During installation, Google Play services temporarily needs a bit of extra headroom to copy the file into place before immediately clearing its download cache.

Meanwhile, Google noted RAM usage is “minimal & transient” as “Android doesn’t load the 3D emoji font file into RAM.” The support page listed 6 GB as a “cutoff to ensure lower-memory devices stay on the lightweight ~3 MB 2D vector font.”.

Noto 3D emoji goes from vector-based 2D emoji to a high-resolution bitmap font. This results in “high-resolution designs” for emoji “with more texture and dimension to characters and icons.” Google has an FAQ section about why the new emoji might look low resolution:.

Sources indicate that vector vs. bitmap rendering: Older Android emoji used 2D vector graphics, which scale infinitely to any size without losing resolution. The 3D emoji are bitmap graphics, which are pre-rendered pixel-based images. When these images are scaled up by an app or zoomed in, the pixels stretch, which can cause a softer or lower-resolution appearance.

The Google support article published this week lists the minimum specs your Android device must have to get 3D emoji:.

Recent findings suggest that the last two bullet points are rather surprising. In fact, Google even lists instructions for checking how much memory and storage your device has:.

In terms of availability, Google says a supported device will “automatically download the 3D emoji when it’s on Wi-Fi and charging.”.

At this time, there isn’t a way to force download the emoji.

In a recent development, google announced 3D emoji in May, with the upcoming design shipping on the Pixel 11 in August. It has since arrived on older Pixel devices.

In terms of OEM availability, Google explicitly indicates “Samsung devices use a proprietary emoji font and do not receive the 3D font update.” Additionally:.

This is also true for third-party messaging apps, such as WhatsApp, who use their own emoji fonts rather than relying on your device’s system font.

The gaming industry is notoriously secretive, and that's doubly true for anything related to Grand Theft Auto 6. Rockstar Games kept much of the game tightly under wraps, including one of the title's biggest secrets — a remarkable feat when you consider how much of the game leaked prior to launch. All of this might be true, but it didn't take the sting out of one husband's recent discovery about his wife's work on the record-breaking open-world title.

Amber Wallin is a comedian who voices several non-playable characters in GTA 6. Wallin's voice can be heard during an early segment of the game where Lucia is notified she will be allowed to carry out her sentence via a quasi-home arrest program. Wallin appears in a few other roles throughout the game, such as a character who roasts Jason after he harasses her.

According to recent reports, given her profession, it's no surprise that Wallin's characters are a hoot. "Motherfucker wanna clock out soon when shit gets real," she says via the aggravated NPC. "Clock in, ho. Time is money!".

It has been revealed that while Wallin's various roles are minor, the game is already the biggest entertainment launch of all time, meaning anyone who can say they were involved in its creation has much to brag about. So, imagine the surprise of Wallin's husband when he learned she was in the game like any other player. According to a video the couple recently posted on social media, Wallin apparently kept her involvement in the game a total secret from even her husband for two years.

"NDAs do not apply to husbands," Wallin's partner screams. The video is not entirely serious — at one point, Wallin suggests Rockstar Games could assassinate her for talking about it even now. The clip was obviously planned beforehand and is staged to look like a dramatic segment in a reality TV show as well. Yet the feelings expressed in it, and Wallin's tight-lipped approach to her work, appear to be 100% genuine.

Perhaps the most ironic part is that Wallin has a video where she playfully describes her relationship with her husband. In it, she describes a time during pregnancy where she took care of a handful of tedious house chores. When she was finished, she wanted to treat herself with a pint of ice cream — but when she opened the fridge, all she found was an empty carton. On top of not throwing it out, the husband evidently did not even bother to put the ice cream back in the freezer.

Given GTA 6's focus on relationships and how much it encourages men to be thoughtful partners, perhaps playing through the game will be instructive and remind Wallin's husband that he has NPCs at home.
